Original Requirements: Act as a Senior Software Engineer and Architect specializing in Rust. Build the "mrk-browser" project, a modular mini-browser in Rust with a hybrid architecture (GUI + TUI) and a rendering pipeline focused on content conversion.
Product Goals: Create a modular application that supports both a GUI and a TUI.
Build an efficient pipeline for converting HTML to MDX.
User Stories: As a user, I want to choose between the graphical interface and the terminal interface to use the browser.
As a developer, I would like the browser to support multiple tabs to make it easier to work with multiple pieces of online content.
As a user, I want a working address bar in the graphical interface so I can easily enter URLs and move between them.
Competitive Analysis: Brave: Privacy-focused browser with extension support.
Firefox Focus: Minimalist browser focused on speed and privacy.
DuckDuckGo Privacy Browser: Browser that puts user privacy ahead of data collection.
Opera: Browser known for its speed and advanced security features.
Vivaldi: Browser with a customizable interface, focused on productivity and user control.

Requirement Analysis: The 'mrk-browser' project requires a modular architecture that allows GUI and TUI integration, plus an efficient pipeline for converting HTML to MDX. The user interface must be intuitive and easy to use, with full address bar support in the GUI.
Requirement Pool: Implement an internal Rust library to manage the network layer (reqwest/tokio).
Build a parser that sanitizes the structural tags and converts the content directly to the MDX format.
Use Tauri to render the default desktop interface in the GUI.
Use Ratatui to provide a full experience directly in the terminal (TUI).
UI Design draft: The user interface must be intuitive, with a modern, minimalist design. The address bar must be present in the GUI to make navigation easier, while the TUI offers a clean, well-organized reading experience.
